# How to Edit Your Phone Photos with Simple Text Instructions in Meta AI

> **In short:** Send Meta AI a photo, type what you want changed ("remove the person on the left", "make the sky look like sunset"), and it returns a new version. Simple edits usually work on the first try; complex changes may need a couple of attempts.

Ever take a great photo and then notice a stranger walking through the background? Or snap a sunset shot where the sky came out dull and gray? You don't have to learn a photo editor to fix these — Meta AI can do small edits just by typing what you want. This guide walks through how, on your phone, in a few minutes.

## Before you start
- A phone with **Meta AI** available — built into WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, or Messenger. If you don't see it in any of those, the same chat works at **meta.ai** in your phone's browser.
- A Meta account (the same one you use for Facebook or Instagram works).
- One photo saved on your phone that you'd like to edit — landscape, portrait, or a quick snapshot, any of them.
- A working internet connection.
- About **5 minutes** for your first edit, and a little patience if the first attempt isn't quite right.

> **One honest note:** Meta AI is great at small, focused edits — sky color, brightness, removing a clear object. It is not a replacement for a full photo editor like Photoshop. If your request is very complex, the result may surprise you, and that's normal.

## Step 1 — Open a chat with Meta AI
Open WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, or Messenger, then find the contact or chat labeled **Meta AI**. It's usually marked with a little blue or purple ring around its profile picture. In WhatsApp, tap the green new-chat button and look for "Meta AI" near the top of your contacts. In Instagram, start a new direct message and search for "Meta AI". A one-on-one chat opens, with a text box at the bottom and a paperclip or **+** button on the left for attaching things. If you can't find Meta AI in any app, open your phone's browser and go to **meta.ai** — sign in with your Facebook or Instagram account if asked, and you'll land in the same chat.
💬 Example: Open WhatsApp → tap the new-chat icon → tap "Meta AI" in the contacts list.
You'll know it worked when a chat thread opens with "Meta AI" at the top and a text box you can type into.

## Step 2 — Send the photo you want to edit
Tap the paperclip, **+**, or camera icon next to the text box, then pick **Photo** or **Gallery** from the menu. Your phone's photo library opens. Select the photo you want — just one to start, so the AI has a clear focus. The photo appears as a small preview in the chat; tap **Send** (the arrow button) to deliver it. The image uploads in a few seconds, and Meta AI now "sees" it. If you're using **meta.ai** in the browser instead, look for an upload icon — usually an arrow pointing up or a small picture frame — on the left side of the message box. Tap it, pick the photo, and send the same way.
💬 Example: One landscape photo where the sky looks flat and gray — perfect for your first edit.
You'll know it worked when your selected photo shows up in the chat as a sent message.

## Step 3 — Type what you want changed
In the text box right below the photo, write a short, plain sentence describing the edit. Tap send. You'll see three small dots animating while Meta AI thinks — that means it's working. Within a few seconds, sometimes up to a minute, it replies with a new image, usually with a one-sentence acknowledgment like "Here's the edited version." The new photo lands in the chat as another message bubble. If the reply is **only text** with no image, your instruction was probably unclear — try again with the wording in the example below.
💬 Example: "Make the sky look like a bright sunset with orange and pink clouds" — or simpler, "Remove the person on the right" or "Brighten the photo so it doesn't look so dark."
You'll know it worked when a new image appears in the chat that looks like your photo, but with the change you asked for.

## Step 4 — Look closely at the edit
Tap the new image to open it full-screen. Pinch out with two fingers to zoom in on the area you asked to change. Now look at it honestly: did the edit land where you wanted? Sometimes Meta AI nails it. Other times the change is subtle, or it shifted something you didn't ask to change — a face looks slightly different, or a building in the background got smudged. That happens, and it doesn't mean you did anything wrong. If the image is small and won't zoom in the chat, take a screenshot of your phone (side button + volume up on most phones) — that captures the full-size version for closer inspection.
💬 Example: Ask yourself — is the person really gone, or is there a faint shadow where they stood? Is the sky the color you wanted, or does it look painted on?
You'll know it worked when you can decide, honestly, whether this version is good enough to keep or whether you'd like to try again.

## Step 5 — Ask for a redo if it's not quite right
If the edit missed the mark, reply in the same chat with a clearer or more focused instruction. Keep the conversation going — Meta AI keeps the photo and your request in context, so you can iterate. Useful phrases: "Try again", "Make it stronger", "Keep everything else exactly the same and only change the sky", or pointing out what went wrong, like "The person is still there — try once more". If the AI keeps misunderstanding after several tries, start a brand new chat, send just the photo again, and write your best, clearest instruction first. Long threads with many edits sometimes confuse the model.
💬 Example: First try didn't remove the person cleanly? Send: "Try again — remove the person on the right side, but keep everything else exactly the same."
You'll know it worked when a new version finally looks like what you wanted — or when you've accepted that this particular edit isn't possible and you'd rather try a different photo.

## Step 6 — Save the photo you like
When you're happy with an edited version, save it to your phone. Tap and hold the image in the chat — a small menu appears with options like **Save**, **Save to Photos**, or **Share**. Tap "Save" and the photo lands in your camera roll or gallery, just like one you took yourself. In some apps you'll see a small downward-arrow icon on the image — tap that instead. In **meta.ai** in the browser, long-press the image (or right-click on a computer) and choose "Save image as". Only save once you're sure — once it's in your camera roll, you can't easily get back to the older versions still sitting in the chat.
💬 Example: Save your favorite version, then close the chat. Your original photo is untouched on your phone, and the edited version is now saved next to it.
You'll know it worked when you open your phone's Photos or Gallery app and see the edited photo sitting there.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking for too many changes at once.** "Remove the person, fix the sky, brighten everything, and add a reflection in the water" is too much for one message. The AI may handle one or two of those, badly, while ignoring the rest. **Fix:** ask for one change at a time, and send the photo back through Step 3 each time.
- **Writing vague instructions.** "Make it better", "fix this", or "improve it" leaves the AI guessing — usually wrong. **Fix:** describe exactly what to change in plain words. "Make the sky bluer" works; "nicer sky" doesn't.
- **Not zooming in to check the result.** On a phone screen, a small image can look fine until you look closely — then you notice a smudged face or a ghostly outline where someone was removed. **Fix:** always open the image full-screen and zoom in on the edited area before saving.
- **Saving the first version without comparing.** The first attempt is rarely the best one. **Fix:** wait until you've tried once or twice and you've got the version you actually want, then save that one.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** vacation photos where someone walked into your shot, birthday candles that came out dim, a beach picture where the sky was gray — all fixable in under a minute with one short instruction.
- **For your business or work:** quick product photos, social media posts, or marketplace listings where the background needs cleanup. Type what you want removed, send it through, save the result. It won't replace a designer, but it gets you 80% of the way in seconds.
- **If you're just getting started:** pick a photo that's been bothering you — maybe a great group shot with a stranger in the corner — and try removing them first. It's the easiest edit to see if Meta AI is working for you.

## Try it now
Open Meta AI right now in WhatsApp, Instagram, or **meta.ai** in your browser. Send one photo you've taken recently — anything from this week. Then type one short instruction, such as "Make the colors look brighter" or "Remove the trash can in the corner". The whole thing takes under two minutes, and you'll see exactly how the tool responds to your wording — which makes the next edit easier too.
